subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed allowed-plus-blocked DNS result sets can proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or keep the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed rule?
rationale: The implementation shape is small, but it changes the default outbound SSRF boundary for web_fetch and must reflect maintainer security intent rather than an automated policy guess.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and test mixed-answer plus all-blocked cases.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat the current strict DNS-answer behavior as intentional and document proxy or fake-IP opt-ins for affected networks.

options.title: Make mixed DNS explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse a named operator-controlled policy for polluted dual-stack DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and test mixed-answer plus all-blocked cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The current SSRF assertion and nearby security-hardening history most directly route the security-boundary choice here.
